findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reframe the commit-message recording sub-requirement as an outcome criterion with a verification path, e.g. 'the PR description or commit footer contains two lines of the form `runner.py before: N LOC` and `runner.py after: M LOC` where M < N and M < 700' — and note that reviewers can grep the commit message to verify.
evidence: 'before/after LOC is MEASURED and recorded in the commit message' — this is an action the committer must take, not a property of the code
There is no test or CI check that would fail if the commit message omits this information
findings.finding: AC6's sub-requirement 'runner.py's before/after LOC is MEASURED and recorded in the commit message' is a one-time process obligation, not a durable observable end-state in the repository — it cannot be verified from the repo artifact alone after the fact without reading commit metadata.
scenarios: Reviewer cannot verify compliance from the PR diff alone; the criterion is satisfied by a commit message that could have been written without actually measuring.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `build_model_settings` and `build_usage_limits` to both the `test_moved_symbols_are_importable_from_the_new_module` and `test_runner_no_longer_defines_the_moved_symbols` checked sets in `test_structured_run_seam.py`, and enumerate that file as an edit target.
evidence: test_moved_symbols_are_importable_from_the_new_module checks only the prior extraction set: _pai_structured, _extract_usage, _warn_if_zeroed_usage, effective_max_iterations, effective_max_tokens
test_runner_no_longer_defines_the_moved_symbols checks the same fixed set
The plan names no update to this file despite requiring that build_model_settings and build_usage_limits land in structured_run.py
findings.finding: test_structured_run_seam.py is not listed as an edit target, but it hardcodes the set of symbols that must be importable from structured_run and must no longer be defined in runner.py — after this extraction both lists need build_model_settings and build_usage_limits added to have teeth.
scenarios: A partial move (e.g. build_model_settings copied but runner.py retains its own inline version) would pass both seam tests silently — exactly the 'copied not moved' failure the seam tests were designed to catch.
If the symbols are named differently from what the plan specifies, the structural guard never fires.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `'build_model_settings'` and `'build_usage_limits'` to the `for name in (...)` tuple in `test_moved_symbols_are_importable_from_the_new_module`, and to the `defined & {...}` set literal in `test_runner_no_longer_defines_the_moved_symbols`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `cache_settings` (or its computed equivalent) to the `build_model_settings` signature — the function's body initializes `model_settings` from `dict(cache_settings)`, so the parameter is load-bearing and must appear in the spec.
evidence: runner.py:408: `model_settings = dict(cache_settings) if cache_settings is not None else {}`
runner.py:381: `cache_settings = None if self._model_override else cache_settings_for(caps)`
Plan scope: `build_model_settings(cfg, req, caps, resolved, *, model_override) -> dict` — no `cache_settings` parameter
structured_run.py has no import from rebar.llm.capabilities — so an internal call to cache_settings_for would add a new dependency without specification
findings.finding: `build_model_settings` signature omits `cache_settings` (the dict base), but the extracted region initializes model_settings as `dict(cache_settings) if cache_settings is not None else {}`. The plan's stated signature `build_model_settings(cfg, req, caps, resolved, *, model_override)` has no slot for `cache_settings`, so the implementer must either add an undocumented parameter or recompute it internally — both diverge from the spec silently.
findings.location: Scope section — function signature `build_model_settings(cfg, req, caps, resolved, *, model_override) -> dict`
scenarios: Implementer omits cache_settings → extracted function always returns a model_settings without cache flags, silently breaking prompt caching for all Anthropic calls
Implementer adds cache_settings parameter ad-hoc → parameter count exceeds ~6 and should per ADR 0056 trigger a carrier, but the spec says not to introduce one
findings.suggested_fix: Signature: `build_model_settings(cfg, req, caps, resolved, cache_settings, *, model_override) -> dict`. If this pushes the positional count past ~6, note the exception explicitly (the carrier ADR threshold is advisory, not hard, when a parameter is genuinely required).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC that explicitly asserts `from rebar.llm.structured_run import build_model_settings, build_usage_limits` succeeds (and optionally that `runner` no longer defines them at module scope), so the extraction destination is directly verified.
evidence: Plan body: 'src/rebar/llm/runner.py ~384-463 -> two plain functions … build_model_settings … build_usage_limits'
Plan body: 'The themed module already exists: src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py'
AC5 checks 'structured_run.py remains under 500 LOC' but not that the named functions exist there
AC6 checks runner.py LOC shrank but not that the destination module received the functions
No AC states 'from rebar.llm.structured_run import build_model_settings, build_usage_limits succeeds'
findings.finding: No acceptance criterion verifies that `build_model_settings` and `build_usage_limits` are importable from `structured_run.py` specifically. AC1–AC3 test behavioral properties of the functions but do not name the import path, so a nominally passing test suite would not catch the functions being placed in the wrong module or left inline.
scenarios: An implementer extracts to a different file and all behavioral tests still pass, leaving AC5/AC6 green while the destination is wrong.
structured_run.py gains unrelated boilerplate to satisfy AC5's LOC floor without the functions actually landing there.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: '- [ ] `from rebar.llm.structured_run import build_model_settings, build_usage_limits` succeeds in a unit-tier import test; runner.py does not define either name at module scope after the extraction.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC (or a note in the commit-message checklist) that the temperature-deprecation-matrix comment block and the per-request-vs-config precedence rationale comment are present verbatim in the extracted module, or are explicitly called out in the PR description as preserved.
evidence: 'The comments TRAVEL WITH the code -- they are the temperature-deprecation matrix and the per-request-vs-config precedence rationale'
'Do not strip them to fit'
'Deleting documentation to satisfy a size guard is the raise the cap anti-pattern ADR 0056 rejects by name'
No AC references comment preservation or character/line count of the comment block
findings.finding: The 'Honest Accounting' section imposes a concrete, named constraint ('comments TRAVEL WITH the code — do not strip them to hit a number') but no AC verifies it; the LOC floor only guards against over-stripping indirectly and is not equivalent.
scenarios: An implementer strips the temperature-deprecation matrix to fit structured_run.py under 500 LOC; all ACs pass but the named invariant is violated.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the `build_usage_limits` return tuple members explicitly — the caller needs all three values `(UsageLimits, req_limit, eff_max_iter)` as post-call locals for `FailureContext` and the telemetry log.
evidence: runner.py:542-543: `FailureContext(req_limit=req_limit, eff_max_iter=eff_max_iter, ...)`
runner.py:572-573: `usage.get('requests', 0), req_limit, eff_max_iter` in the logger.info call
runner.py:476-480: req_limit and eff_max_iter are computed inside the region being extracted
Plan scope: `build_usage_limits(cfg, req, UsageLimits) -> tuple` — no tuple member specification
findings.finding: `build_usage_limits` is specified to return `tuple` but the tuple's shape is not defined, yet the caller (`run()`) needs `req_limit` and `eff_max_iter` as separate locals after the call — they populate `FailureContext.req_limit`, `FailureContext.eff_max_iter`, and the telemetry `logger.info` at lines 572–573. An underspecified return leaves the implementer to guess and risks those values being unavailable post-extraction.
scenarios: Implementer returns only `(UsageLimits,)` → run() can't populate FailureContext.req_limit / eff_max_iter without re-deriving them, defeating the extraction
Implementer returns `(UsageLimits, req_limit)` omitting eff_max_iter → telemetry log line silently uses a stale or recomputed value
findings.suggested_fix: Return type annotation: `-> tuple[UsageLimits, int, int]` where the members are `(usage_limits, req_limit, eff_max_iter)`. Document this in the scope section.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a proving command to AC7: specify a grep/AST scan (e.g. `grep -rn 'monkeypatch.setattr.*runner' tests/`) that enumerates ALL existing runner-targeted patches before extraction, so the executor can confirm each one is either irrelevant to the moved region or has been repointed.
evidence: Body prose: 'Run the full suite and repoint what breaks' — conditional on breakage, not a positive assertion
No command is specified to enumerate monkeypatch targets in the moved region before and after extraction
'I re-exported it is never evidence a repoint was unneeded' — plan acknowledges the risk but provides no proving command to rule it out
findings.finding: AC7 ('any monkeypatch target that moved is repointed IN THE SAME COMMIT and named in the message') has no concrete in-plan proving command; the body says 'run the full suite and repoint what breaks,' but that is a hedge, not a deterministic check — a repoint that is missing but happens not to be exercised by the test suite would silently pass.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC7; 'Monkeypatch repoints — measure, do NOT assume zero' section
scenarios: A monkeypatch.setattr('runner._pai_model', ...) remains unbroken at test time (the test doesn't invoke the extracted path), the repoint is skipped, and a future integration test fails with a misleading error.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC (and corresponding seam-test stub or parameterisation) that applies the same leaf invariant (no runtime import from runner) and LOC guards to any second themed module created under the split path.
evidence: 'If both functions plus their travelling comments would breach 500, split along a real seam into a second themed module at or above the 100-LOC floor'
No corresponding requirement to add a seam test or leaf-invariant assertion for the new module
test_structured_run_seam.py::test_structured_run_has_no_runtime_import_from_runner covers only structured_run.py by name — a new sibling module is unguarded
findings.finding: If the extraction breaches 500 LOC and a second themed module is created, the plan specifies no leaf invariant, no seam test, and no documentation requirement for that module — so the runtime-import-from-runner prohibition and LOC bounds that protect structured_run.py would have no enforcement on the new module.
findings.location: Section 'Destination and its headroom' — fallback split path; AC line 'the extracted module is at or above the 100-LOC anti-fragmentation floor'
scenarios: Developer hits the 500-LOC ceiling and splits; the new module silently imports runner at runtime; no test catches it; the leaf invariant is violated without CI feedback
A future extraction targets the new module without knowing it lacks LOC or import constraints, compounding technical debt
findings.suggested_fix: Extend test_structured_run_seam.py to parameterise the runtime-import check over all modules in the run-execution cluster (or list the second module explicitly if created), and add an AC: 'if a second module is created, test_structured_run_seam.py is updated in the same commit to enforce its leaf invariant and LOC bounds'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Spell out the call-site pattern for `build_usage_limits`: confirm that `run()` retains `from pydantic_ai.usage import UsageLimits` (already lazy inside run()) and passes the class object as the third positional argument, so structured_run.py itself never imports pydantic_ai.
evidence: runner.py:234: `from pydantic_ai.usage import UsageLimits` is a lazy import inside run()
structured_run.py must not import pydantic_ai at module top (leaf invariant enforced by test_structured_run_has_no_runtime_import_from_runner)

The plan states the signature but gives no description of whether run() passes `UsageLimits` as the class object, and does not address whether the TYPE_CHECKING annotation for the return type `tuple` needs further elaboration (e.g. `tuple[UsageLimits, int, int]`)
findings.finding: The plan specifies `build_usage_limits(cfg, req, UsageLimits) -> tuple` — passing the pydantic-ai `UsageLimits` class as a parameter to keep structured_run.py a leaf — but never describes how run() retains its lazy `from pydantic_ai.usage import UsageLimits` import and passes the class through, leaving the call-site plumbing ambiguous for the implementer.
findings.location: Scope section — `build_usage_limits(cfg, req, UsageLimits) -> tuple` signature; runner.py:234 (`from pydantic_ai.usage import UsageLimits`)
scenarios: An implementer naively adds `from pydantic_ai.usage import UsageLimits` at the top of structured_run.py to satisfy the function body — the leaf test fails.
An implementer moves the lazy import inside build_usage_limits — the function is no longer pure (it still imports) and may not match the plan's implied purity.

findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC6: 'this commit independently leaves runner.py under the 700 headroom guard'
scenarios: Executor completes the extraction, CI passes for unrelated reasons, and runner.py silently breaches 700 LOC because no test or CI step actually asserts the threshold.
